featured_reviews.name: vishal bhagdev
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the most authentic South Indian meal experiences I've had. The entire 23-item spread was served with so much warmth and attention to detail. Every dish had its own flavour and uniqueness - nothing felt repetitive or heavy. The gunpowder idli was bursting with flavour, the pineapple shira was perfectly balanced, and the payasam was the ideal sweet finish. What impressed me even more was that the entire team travelled all the way from Mumbai to Surendranagar for the wedding and still delivered such consistent quality. Truly homely, traditional, and delicious. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Kale
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shree Dharma Saasta caterers were tasked to cater for a family wedding in early February. The entire team came to Hyderabad from Mumbai. They served breakfast, lunch, evening tiffin and dinner on day 1 followed by breakfast and lunch on day 2.  Except for day 1 dinner , the rest of the meals were authentic South Indian delicacies.

Everything in each meal was excellent. The idli on day 1 was outstanding, something different than normal idli you would usually have.

Day 1 reception buffet was an excellent blend of variety, from chat dishes to main course.

A small observation nevertheless!!

The serving staff can perhaps take a cue of what to serve when  eg. You are towards the end of your breakfast and some stewards were lining up offering to serve idli podi (if you know South Indian meal order, you would know generally what item gets consumed when). Or circling around asking for serving sambar ( in addition )when you are asking for payasam!!

Overall, these little things don't change the fact that food was amazing.

Good job Chandru and team!

featured_reviews.name: Karthik Ramanadhan
featured_reviews.review_text: We attended a wedding very recently, during which Nirmalyam were the caterers for kalyanam food. Taste-wise Nirmalyam deserves the appreciation. However on grounds of service, cleanliness, hygiene and hospitality Nirmalyam failed to uphold their food taste quality. It seems they have employed unprofessional people or/and the supervision is lacking. Quality control is absolutely lacking in the kitchen and service area and it shows during the delivery and some items of food like curd and sambhar and rasam. During sadhya, serving the food needs to be done quick and cleanly initially. And whenever the item is refused the server needs to move on as well as be ready to serve it again on request. Serving hot dishes in the beginning itself isn't a very good practice as Indian food needs to eaten hot if ever we want to get the proper taste. We would never engage them in any more functions.

featured_reviews.name: Rathi Harikrishnan
featured_reviews.review_text:
My family was one of the earliest patrons of Nirmalyam when Mr. Suresh had just started out in the field (in the early 2000s). At that time, his focus was on delivering quality. That showed in his service! Food used to be excellent. He quickly dethroned the reigning caterers such as Ronak and went on to expand on a very large scale. My own wedding, my brother's upanayanam, and my cousin's wedding have been catered by Nirmalyam. There was a time when their food and service were excellent.
However, success and large-scale expansion have exacted a heavy price. I have attended at least 5 recent events- engagements and weddings, a few in my family itself- and the food has been unpalatable! Nothing was tasty. Chutney has been consistently putrid, sambar awful, Idli sour. It's shameful. Now since he has monopoly in South Indian, Tamilian weddings, it's unfortunate that unsuspecting families are subjected to his shoddy service. I hope anyone who enlists his catering services, thoroughly checks and thinks at least twice before asking Nirmalyam to cater such important events in their lives!
